title: Light My Fire and the crossover backlash
summary: The 1969 Cadet album with Light My Fire was the band's first crossover; it sold well but angered old fans.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Just wanted to swing back a little bit. Let's see, I have a note here. You began to move
into broader range of material, I think, with Cadet Records and "Light My Fire."
That was our first crossover, if you can call it that.
Yeah, yeah. You had all kinds of reaction to that.
Yeah, a lot good. We sold a lot of it. It was one of our more important albums. And a lot of hate came out of our old bands.
They said, "What are you doing, deserting us?"
You're doing my song. Or, what they hoped would never be their song.
But I -- fortunately, that acts as an encouragement to me. I'm a very stubborn man, and when I get a lot of opposition, I work harder.
That's interesting. Did that present problems for you at all in, say, the first exposure and bookings and things? People saying, "that's not what I expected to hear."
Sure, very often it does. But I try to be as forceful and strong about it as I can. Also, for each step forward, you take a half step back. You're never really
that revolutionary, it's that some people don't want any kind of progress, in anything.
No. 'Let it be the way it always was, the good old days. Which is tomorrow.
